page: Oracle Cloud Infrastructure VM.Standard.A2.Flex.32-128 is an Arm-based compute instance built on the Ampere AmpereOne processor architecture. The instance is configured with 64 dedicated physical cores operating at a base frequency of 3.0 GHz. Because the Ampere architecture implements a single thread per physical core, the instance provides 64 dedicated vCPUs with zero hyperthreading contention. Complementing the processor cores is 128.0 GB of system memory, establishing a 1:2 core-to-memory ratio of 2.0 GB of RAM per vCPU.

The instance does not include integrated local NVMe storage, requiring persistent storage to be attached via remote block storage volumes over the network. Hardware accelerators are absent, with zero GPUs allocated. Networking capabilities include one complimentary public IPv4 address. The absence of SMT guarantees predictable core execution times across multithreaded jobs, though workloads requiring heavy SIMD extensions must account for the lack of x86-specific instruction sets like AVX-512.

From a cost-efficiency perspective, the AmpereOne platform provides high compute density and execution consistency at a competitive operating footprint compared to traditional x86 server classes. VM.Standard.A2.Flex.32-128 is suited for horizontally scalable compute tasks, continuous integration and build pipelines, Arm software compilation, containerized microservices, and compute-bound API serving architectures.
description: Oracle Cloud Infrastructure VM.Standard.A2.Flex.32-128 is an Arm-based virtual machine powered by Ampere AmpereOne processors running at 3.0 GHz. The configuration allocates 64 dedicated physical cores and 64 vCPUs without multithreading, providing deterministic single-threaded core execution. The system features 128.0 GB of RAM, offering a 1:2 vCPU-to-memory ratio of 2.0 GB per core. The instance includes no integrated local storage or hardware accelerators, requiring external network block storage for persistent data requirements. Network configuration provides one complimentary public IPv4 address. By offering high core density and uniform core execution, the instance presents an efficient hardware profile for compute-centric, scale-out environments. VM.Standard.A2.Flex.32-128 is suited for native Arm application compilation, CI/CD workloads, containerized backend services, and distributed compute clusters.
